case.pattern_description: The undocumented pattern consists of multiple unrelated cards being used to make online purchases directed to a single recipient email domain, sc.rr.com. This pattern affects 17 different cards and indicates a coordinated fraud ring funneling funds to a common destination. It was discovered by analyzing recipient activity, which showed an abnormal spike in the number of unique cards paying this domain over a 30-day period.

evidence.claim: This card's online purchase(s) ($305.41, $366.35, $295.92) went to recipient e-mail domain sc.rr.com, which 17 different cards paid in the 30 days before this case, against a median of 2 card(s) a month in the earlier months it was paid at all: many cards paying one recipient

The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.067, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8

Containment plan for the analyst (this case's own actions cover only its card): the 17-card ring has $7,612.44 at risk. Blocking 16 card(s) (C01727-K2, C04668-K1, C01357-K1, C02167-K2, C05610-K1, C01594-K1, C03060-K1, C11617-K1, ...) would cut 98.4% of it, and the other 1 would be monitored. Blocking every ring card would cut 100.0% but is expected to block 3.5 customer(s) who are not compromised, against 3.0 for this plan. Blocked at under 0.9 confidence, named for review: C04668-K1, C01357-K1, C02167-K2, C05610-K1, C01594-K1, C03060-K1, C11617-K1, C00534-K2, C10350-K1, C01507-K1, C06115-K1, C06639-K1, C11940-K1, C04146-K1, C08384-K1.

case.summary: This alert was triggered by an analyst request to review transaction 3660263 on card C01727-K2 and identify commonalities among affected cards. Graph evidence revealed that 17 different cards made payments to the same recipient email domain, sc.rr.com, within a 30-day period. The policy engine reached a verdict of fraud. Final actions include automatically creating a case, monitoring connected cards, and escalating to an analyst, along with an L1 recommendation to block the card and an L2 recommendation to file a suspicious activity report.

sar.narrative: This report details suspicious online activity involving customer C01727 and their card C01727-K2. Between 2017-01-17 and 2017-01-28, the card was used for three online purchases totaling $967.68. The transactions occurred as follows: transaction 3660261 on 2017-01-17 for $305.41, transaction 3660262 on 2017-01-18 for $366.35, and transaction 3660263 on 2017-01-28 for $295.92. All of these transactions were directed to the recipient email domain sc.rr.com. This activity is highly suspicious because graph analysis indicates that 17 different cards have made payments to this specific email domain in the past 30 days, compared to a historical median of just 2 cards per month. This sudden concentration of unrelated cards paying a single recipient domain strongly suggests a coordinated fraud ring. The total exposure for this specific card is $967.68, while the broader ring poses a risk of $7,612.44.
